content.value_statement: Teams need legal context when prioritizing web accessibility work. This public guide helps frame ADA exposure, remediation priorities, and documentation drafts for professional review.
actual_capabilities: Provides discussion topics for ADA Title II, Title III, Section 508, and California Unruh Act exposure.
Highlights keyboard traps, missing form labels, missing alternative text, and inaccessible popups as accessibility review priorities.
Frames requests for US accessibility statements and remediation plans.
Provides an example demand-letter scenario for an online store and identifies issues for counsel to review.
Identifies municipal portals and federal vendor accessibility as distinct planning scenarios.
limitations: The package contains only a public Markdown guide, not scripts, extension source, or documentation templates.
No executable audit engine or complete 50-point checklist is included, despite the guide describing those features.
Outputs require counsel review; the claimed legal fact base and continuing regulatory updates are not supplied or independently verified.
The guide focuses on WCAG 2.1 AA and does not provide comprehensive WCAG 2.2 coverage.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Storefront Accessibility Work
use_cases.description: Use reported checkout and navigation barriers to prepare a remediation discussion that separates technical findings from legal assumptions.

use_cases.title: Scope a Municipal Portal Review
use_cases.description: Organize accessibility evidence and questions about Title II applicability and current deadlines before consulting authoritative sources.

use_cases.title: Prepare Documentation for Counsel
use_cases.description: Draft an accessibility statement or demand-letter response outline using verified organizational facts and clearly identified uncertainties.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Initial Review Topics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this guide to suggest accessibility review topics for [website type]. Separate technical checks from legal questions and identify missing information.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Observed Barriers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these observed barriers: [findings]. Suggest WCAG 2.1 AA remediation priorities, user impacts, and verification steps. Do not invent test results.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Accessibility Statement
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an accessibility statement for [organization] using [verified findings], [contact details], and [remediation commitments]. Mark unknowns and require counsel review.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Exposure Review Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a counsel-review brief for [organization type], [jurisdiction], [site functions], and [demand-letter allegations]. Separate ADA applicability questions, evidence, remediation options, and unverified deadlines.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate legal and technical review

output_examples.input: Our checkout has unlabeled inputs and a popup that traps keyboard focus. Suggest a remediation sequence.
output: Address both reported barriers promptly because they may prevent checkout completion.
Associate visible labels with inputs and verify their accessible names.
Correct popup focus handling and confirm that keyboard users can close the popup and continue checkout.
Record manual test evidence before claiming the barriers are resolved.

output_examples.input: We manage a municipal portal. What should our accessibility review brief contain?
output: Record the entity type, portal functions, and affected public services.
Ask counsel to verify Title II applicability and the current compliance deadline against authoritative sources.
Summarize observed barriers, affected users, responsible teams, and proposed remediation dates.
Distinguish confirmed test results from assumptions and untested areas.

best_practices: Provide organizational facts, jurisdiction, and observed accessibility evidence before requesting exposure analysis.
Verify legal requirements and deadlines with current authoritative sources and qualified counsel.
Validate proposed fixes through manual keyboard testing, assistive technology testing, and appropriate automated checks.
anti_patterns: Treating generated legal explanations as definitive advice or a guarantee against litigation.
Claiming an automated audit or complete checklist was supplied by this guide.
Publishing accessibility claims or regulatory deadlines without verifying their accuracy.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. The guide explicitly requires counsel review, and generated drafts do not establish legal compliance.

faq.question: Can this package automatically audit my website?
faq.answer: No audit engine is included. The guide can frame review requests, but actual testing requires separate tools and manual evaluation.

faq.question: What files and assets are included?
faq.answer: Only SKILL.md is supplied. Scripts, extension source, documentation templates, and a complete 50-point checklist are not included.

faq.question: Does it cover WCAG 2.2?
faq.answer: The guide focuses on WCAG 2.1 AA. Use additional resources when WCAG 2.2 coverage is required.

faq.question: Are the legal claims and deadlines verified?
faq.answer: The supplied package contains no supporting legal database or update mechanism. Verify its claims against current authoritative sources.

faq.question: Can I use this guide with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: These tools can use the Markdown guide as context. Platform support does not add the missing scripts, templates, or audit engine.
